Hi Hannah & Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our current reference architecture for embedding Redwood into Starlit Assist (PDF attached). High level context: we want to embed Redwood-hosted or dedicated inference behind our orchestration layer so customers get a managed assistant with predictable latency and tenant isolation.

Primary asks:
- Quick pass on the reference design: major gaps or red flags?
- Confirmation of supported deployment modes for the patterns shown (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC).
- A test plan or validation steps we should run during the POC.

Traffic profile: expect ~150–300 QPS for multi-tenant staging, spikes to 600 QPS for short bursts; typical prompt length 80–200 tokens, ~20% of requests are chat-style conversational sequences with KV cache reuse. SLO: p95 < 150ms for simple generations, p95 < 500ms for multi-turn chat (target).

I've attached starlit-reference-architecture.pdf. Procurement is looped in so we can align on commercial/contract questions later.

Appreciate any early feedback — happy to set up a technical readout this week.

Cheers,

Daniel — quick technical notes from a compatibility pass: 
- KV cache expectations: your reference calls out session affinity to an upstream cache. For multi-turn chat we need to ensure the upstream routing preserves KV affinity or use Redwood prefix caching; otherwise you will see cold-start token penalties.
- Quantization & model variants: Redwood supports int8/4-bit runtimes and will expose model profiles; if Starlit plans to run on-prem in the future, we should align on quantized model artifacts (format & validation).
- Batching behavior: with target p95 latency budgets, aggressive batching may hurt tail latency for short requests. We'll include batching configuration suggestions for the POC.
- Security: if you require VPC + HSM-based key management for customer keys, Markus should validate the network diagram and KMS flow.

Can you attach a short CSV with request size distribution and a sample chat session export? That will let us run a better latency simulation before the call.

I'll draft a short test matrix (smoke, perf, soak, correctness) and share it in the Drive link once ready.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

- We do not plan to ship our own quantized weights initially — we'll rely on Redwood's quantized runtime and model variants. We may evaluate local quantization later.

Daniel / team — good progress. After reviewing the artifacts (thanks for the CSV and test plan) here's a concise next-steps plan so we can move to a POC quickly:

Phase 1 — Design gap analysis (this thread): owners & due dates
- Marissa: publish a 1-page gap summary vs your reference (focus: KV cache, batching, latency tail effects) — due Mon 2026-08-16
- Karthik: validate runtime knobs required for your workload (batch size caps, cache TTL suggestions, quantization profiles) — due Mon 2026-08-16
- Markus: high-level network/KMS checklist for Dedicated -> Private transition — due Tue 2026-08-17

Phase 2 — Smoke POC (2 weeks)

Phase 3 — Perf soak & handoff (2–4 weeks)
- Longer soak, failure injection, SLA baseline, and canary plan for customer rollout.
